title: DISCLOSURE_POLICY says crypto-erasure is available; no builtin performs it
claim: Section 3 lists crypto-erasure as available, but no builtin erases or re-wraps a record key; the only route is deleting key files by hand.
evidence: No erase/destroy builtin in builtin/record.go or builtin/case_key.go; the builtin registry has none.
fix_proposal: Stage E7: record_erase and case_key_erase, and rewrite sections 3 and 7 to state exactly what each destroys and what it cannot reach.

title: A Withdrawal records no authority
claim: DISCLOSURE_POLICY says a withdrawal records on whose authority it was made; the Withdrawal node gets only WITHDREW and PERFORMED_BY edges.
evidence: disclosureWriteWithdrawal writes no AUTHORISED_BY edge and no authority property.
fix_proposal: Stage E1: disclose_withdraw takes {authorised_by}; the Withdrawal gets an AUTHORISED_BY edge to the authority's Actor node and the role recorded.

title: The disclosure guard's file list omits two files that hold key material
claim: builtin/custody.go (caseKey, classTagKey) and case_key_passphrase.go are not in DisclosureFiles, so the no-plaintext-rendering guard does not look at them, and nothing detects an omission.
evidence: DisclosureFiles lists 13 files; neither is among them.
fix_proposal: Add both, and add TestEveryFileHoldingKeyMaterialIsGuarded so a file handling key material cannot be left off the list.

title: db_add_relation never persists its relation label
claim: The relation string goes only to an in-memory timeline that db_close clears; the stored edge is a plain DATA edge with no properties, while GRAPH_DATABASE.md says nodes are linked with a string relation label.
evidence: DbAddRelation (builtin/db_wrappers.go:72) calls AddEdge with no properties.
fix_proposal: Stage D2: one transaction adds the edge and indexes relation on it; db_relations reads it back; the CHANGELOG says labels on existing stores were never written.

title: The language server told editors it was version 0.1.0
claim: serverInfo.version was the constant 0.1.0, which no release of the language or the extension ever had, while mlsp --version printed global.Version.
repro: TestInitializeAdvertisesMVPCapabilities asserts ServerInfo.Version == global.Version and fails against the constant.
fix_proposal: serverVersion reads global.Version.

title: net_syn_scan is called deprecated but not marked deprecated
claim: The alias is documented as deprecated, but its metadata carries no StabilityDeprecated, so the editor's builtinDeprecated diagnostic never fires for it.
evidence: No builtin is marked StabilityDeprecated; the deprecated-builtin analyzer test self-skips.
fix_proposal: Mark it StabilityDeprecated with DeprecatedBy net_connect_scan and a stated removal version (3.0).

title: SECURITY.md named 2.4.x as the supported release
claim: The supported-versions table said 2.4.x was current a release after 2.5.0 shipped.
repro: TestSecurityPolicySupportsThisMinor fails against the old table.
fix_proposal: The table names the current minor; the version test holds it to global.Version.

title: Example READMEs taught mutant run with -pwd
claim: Three READMEs taught the legacy run alias and the deprecated -pwd flag, which puts the password in the process table.
fix_proposal: Teach mutant gen --src and a prompt, --password-file or --password-stdin.

title: Four source comments cited a design note that does not exist
claim: dap/protocol.go, dap/session.go, generator/generate.go and vm/debugger.go cited plans/T1_DEBUGGER.md, which exists nowhere and would be gitignored if it did.
evidence: plans/ is in .gitignore; no such file exists locally either.
repro: TestCitedPathsExist fails on all four comments.
fix_proposal: Point them at the sections of docs/DEBUGGING.md that state the same decisions.

title: Analyzer comments state builtin counts three releases old
claim: Comments in hover_card.go, builtin_types.go, language_teach.go, builtin_pair_return.go, unchecked_error.go and webrepl/browser_safe.go quote 399, 409 or 459 builtins in the present tense; the registry holds 659.
evidence: git grep for the numbers in those files.
fix_proposal: State the property instead of a count, or derive the count at runtime.

title: Two roadmap-era documents describe the tree as it was planned
claim: IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE says tests cover env combinations, which the configuration policy forbids; SECURITY_ENHANCEMENTS lists shipped items (--seed, sweep levels) as planned.
fix_proposal: Rewrite both against the tree, or archive them with a banner (owner's call at checkpoint B).

title: Anti-tamper probes route to a detail that says not implemented yet
claim: Unrouted probes report AntiTamperDetailNotImplemented, a probe result that describes an absence of implementation rather than a measurement.
fix_proposal: Implement each routed probe or remove it from routing; nothing reports a result it did not measure.

title: Bytecode is read with no size cap
claim: The artifact decode path reads its input with io.ReadAll and no bound, so an oversized or crafted artifact is loaded whole before anything checks it.
fix_proposal: Bound the read with a named limit and refuse beyond it.

title: 2.5.0 promised bare --password would be refused in the next minor
claim: The warning, main.go help, README.md:130 and CONFIGURATION_POLICY.md:174 all say --password will require --password-insecure in the next minor release; 2.6.0 is that release.
evidence: Promise added in 051045d, shipped in v2.5.0.
repro: mutant x.mu --password p warns and runs.
fix_proposal: Refuse bare --password, naming --password-insecure, --password-file and --password-stdin; reword the four texts as done.

title: A crash during sealing leaves a torn record under its final name
claim: recordWriteFile creates the final path with O_EXCL and removes it only on a reported error, so a killed process leaves a partial .mrec where a complete one is expected; key files already write to a temporary file, sync and rename.
fix_proposal: Seal to a temporary file, fsync, rename; a crash-child test proves no torn record survives.

title: Type uses across modules never reach the symbol graph
claim: lookupType is file-local, so a struct literal or enum reference to a type declared in another module is recorded as unbound and gets no USES_TYPE edge, although the compiler resolves it.
evidence: sema/graph_walk.go:378 notes UnboundType; the compiler resolves across the program in compile order.
fix_proposal: Stage D5: resolve such uses at export in compile order and count what cannot be resolved.

title: db_bfs and db_shortest_path misread their arguments
claim: An unknown direction silently means both; parallel edges are lost; neither walk has a budget; db_shortest_path ignores direction and returns an error where its metadata says an empty result.
fix_proposal: Stage D4: refuse a bad direction or negative depth, budget both walks, return every edge in the walked direction, correct the metadata.

title: Two ledger reads can be silently wrong
claim: ledger_query_nodes on a key that was never indexed returns an empty result with no error; ledger_path uses an undirected search and never says a hop ran against its edge.
evidence: builtin/ledger_read.go:611 and :1211-1249; graphene v0.9.0 dijkstra is undirected.
fix_proposal: Refuse or flag an unindexed key; mark each reversed hop.

title: The label table is rewritten and fsynced on every disclosure write
claim: DeclareTypeNames runs on every disclosure, withdrawal and reclassification write, and graphene rewrites graphene.labels unconditionally.
fix_proposal: Declare the type names once per ledger session.

title: graph export drops the store's Close error
claim: An export that fails to close its store reports success.
fix_proposal: Return the Close error.

title: Unclosed graph handles live until the process exits
claim: A script that forgets db_close or ledger_close leaves the store open until exit, and the next open reports an unclean shutdown; the only sweep is test-only.
fix_proposal: Close open handles at program exit with a warning naming each.

title: db_add_node on an exported symbol store writes nodes the query side cannot decode
claim: graphene's label registry is process-global; custom type 0 is db_* DATA and also the symbol graph's Module, so db_open_disk on an exported store writes Module-labelled nodes that loadModules then fails to decode.
fix_proposal: A policy test that no two graph families give one label number two names, and db_open_disk refuses a symbol store for writing.

title: db_* properties can be written and indexed but never read by key
claim: Scripts can index node properties but have no builtin to look a node up by one.
fix_proposal: Stage D3: db_find, db_node, db_relations, db_schema.

title: The CHANGELOG misdates 2.5.0 and files its entries under Unreleased
claim: [2.5.0] is dated 2026-09-14 but the tag was made 2026-09-17; thirteen [Unreleased] entries (Sigma, C-1, C-2, ED-3, ED-4, the CI removal and others) shipped in that tag; 14d4ea5 and a901ce4 have no entry; the deps entry says graphene v0.9.0 was already current when 2.5.0 shipped v0.4.0.
evidence: git log -1 --format=%ci v2.5.0; git merge-base --is-ancestor for each entry's commit.
repro: git merge-base --is-ancestor f5fd64c v2.5.0 exits 0 while the Sigma entry sits under [Unreleased].
fix_proposal: Move the entries, re-date 2.5.0 to 2026-09-17, add the missing entries, correct the graphene line; the release gate checks the heading date against the tag.
regression_test: scripts/release_gate step: CHANGELOG date matches the tag; cmd/gendocs TestChangelogLeadsWithThisVersion

title: A MODULES.md example used a comment syntax Mutant does not have
claim: The private-names example elided its bodies with /* ... */, which does not parse, so a reader pasting it got a syntax error.
evidence: parse: no prefix parse function for /
fix_proposal: Give the example real bodies.

title: Two links into the capability reference pointed at anchors that no longer exist
claim: SECURE_NETWORKING linked #network-32 and TESTING linked #testing; the headings carry the current counts (#network-33, #testing-10).
fix_proposal: Point at the current anchors; the link test catches the next drift.

title: CONTRIBUTING pointed at the packaging script's old location
claim: scripts/package-targets.mjs lives at mutant-vscode-extension/scripts/package-targets.mjs.
fix_proposal: Cite the real path.

title: Four example programs were reachable from no README
claim: examples/README.md never named collections/, crypto/ or structured/, and the evidence README never named its own export_mft.mut; the old test only looked at top-level directories that had a README.
repro: TestEveryExampleIsListedInItsReadme, now recursive, fails on all four.
fix_proposal: List them; the test now walks every directory and checks the reverse.

title: The example sweep passes --password, which 2.6.0 will refuse
claim: compile, execute and startAndStop all pass --password; once bare --password is refused the whole sweep fails.
fix_proposal: Pass --password-insecure (the explicit opt-in) in the same change that refuses bare --password.

title: LuaPatch carried a field nothing set, which storage dropped anyway
claim: DecryptedChecksum was documented as set after decryption for validation, but no code set or read it, and mutil.EncryptObject/DecryptObject rebuilt LuaPatch without it, so it could not have survived a store in any case.
evidence: git grep DecryptedChecksum finds only the declaration; runtime/lua/lua.go:46 validates against ChecksumExpected.
repro: TestEveryObjectFieldSurvivesStorage fails: DecryptedChecksum stored, loaded empty.
fix_proposal: Remove the field; say where validation really happens.
